cases.case_summary: A 42-year-old man presents with a six-month history of persistent, progressively enlarging swelling of the right thigh and cramping pain over the swelling while walking.
cases.full_text:
A 42-year-old man presents with a six-month history of persistent, progressively enlarging swelling of the right thigh and cramping pain over the swelling while walking.
Prior care and associated history: Conservative pain-relief treatment had been given at two primary healthcare facilities after a misdiagnosis. There was no sudden enlargement, trauma, or similar past lesions, and no fever, chills, or difficulty at work.
Physical examination: General examination was unremarkable. A 12 × 9 × 7 cm firm, tender swelling was present on the outer aspect of the middle third of the right thigh, with pain worse while walking. The overlying skin was normal and movement was unrestricted.
X-ray of the right thigh: AP and lateral views showed no bone involvement, and the swelling was confined to the muscular compartment.
Ultrasound of the right thigh: A 12 × 8 × 8 cm complex, multiloculated cystic lesion in the middle third of the right thigh involved the vastus lateralis muscle belly.
MRI of the right thigh: A cystic lesion with multiple internal daughter cysts measured 13.5 × 6.7 × 5.1 cm and involved the vastus lateralis. It was hypointense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images.
Chest X-ray and ultrasound of the abdomen and pelvis: No additional foci were seen in the chest, abdomen, or pelvis.
Gross inspection of the excised specimen: Multiple daughter cysts were present when the specimen was opened.
cases.final_diagnosis: Intra-muscular hydatid cyst (right thigh) due to Echinococcus granulosus.

cases.case_summary: A 60-year-old woman presented to the surgical outpatient department with anorectal bleeding, loose stools, and perianal pain for the past six months.
cases.full_text:
A 60-year-old woman presented to the surgical outpatient department with anorectal bleeding, loose stools, and perianal pain for the past six months.
Colonoscopy: Nodular ulcerative growth at 7 o'clock, 2 cm from the lower edge of the anal canal.
Tumor cell morphology: Highly pleomorphic polygonal to elongated spindle cells with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, moderate eosinophilic cytoplasm, round-oval to irregular hyperchromatic nuclei, inconspicuous nucleoli, and 4-5 atypical mitoses per 10 high-power fields.
Masson Fontana stain: Tumor cells negative.
S-100, HMB-45, and Melan-A immunohistochemistry: Positive in tumor cells.
Vimentin immunohistochemistry: Diffuse, strong positivity.
Synaptophysin immunohistochemistry: Positive in tumor cells.
PAN-CK and CK-20 immunohistochemistry: Negative.
Oncology evaluation: Widespread and extensive distant metastasis to the lungs, liver, and skeletal system.
cases.final_diagnosis: Amelanotic malignant melanoma with atypical neuroendocrine differentiation of the anorectal region, accompanied by widespread distant metastasis.

cases.case_summary: A 35-year-old primigravida at 39 weeks of gestation presented with decreased fetal movements and underwent emergency cesarean section, during which a right-sided ovarian cyst was found and removed.
cases.full_text:
A 35-year-old primigravida at 39 weeks of gestation presented with decreased fetal movements and underwent emergency cesarean section, during which a right-sided ovarian cyst was found and removed.
Presenting history: 35-year-old primigravida at 39 weeks of gestation with decreased fetal movements
Intraoperative inspection: Right-sided complex ovarian cyst noted and removed
Gross examination: Cystic structure measuring 10x7x5 cm, with mixed solid and cystic areas filled with pultaceous material admixed with hair
Cyst wall histopathology: Ovarian cyst wall lined by stratified squamous epithelium with underlying sebaceous glands, apocrine acini, fatty tissue, smooth muscle, and glial tissue
Glandular tissue histopathology: Mammary tissue with hyperplastic acini and central dilated ducts filled with eosinophilic secretions in multiple lobules, lined by one to two layers of low columnar epithelium with round nuclei and inconspicuous nucleoli, plus secretory vacuoles and luminal secretions
Neural tissue histopathology: Glial tissue with choroidal plexus in a few sections
Estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor immunohistochemistry: Luminal and ductal nuclear positivity
p63 and pan-cytokeratin immunohistochemistry: Strong p63 expression in myoepithelial cells and strong pan-cytokeratin expression in luminal cells
cases.final_diagnosis: Mature cystic teratoma with lactating adenoma arising in the ovary and containing rare findings of choroidal plexus.

cases.case_summary: A 29-year-old woman at 38 weeks and 1 day of gestation presented for confinement.
cases.full_text:
A 29-year-old woman at 38 weeks and 1 day of gestation presented for confinement.
Obstetric history: G5P1L1A3, with a previous lower-segment cesarean section
Maternal blood group and crossmatch: Group A, RhD-positive; crossmatch incompatible, with a compatible unit identified after six units were tested
Maternal direct Coombs test, autocontrol, and indirect Coombs test: Direct Coombs test and autocontrol negative; indirect Coombs test positive
Maternal antibody identification, Duffy phenotype, and titer: 2+ reactivity in panel cells 1, 3, 6, 9, 10, and 11; anti-Fya identified; maternal red cells Fya-b+; anti-Fya titer 8
Paternal red-cell Duffy typing: Fya+b+
Newborn examination at delivery: Live female infant weighing 2.75 kg; APGAR 8/10 at one minute and 9/10 at five minutes; pink and alert, no hydrops, and no abnormality on systemic examination
Cord-blood grouping, direct Coombs test, phenotype, and eluate: Group A, RhD positive; polyspecific direct Coombs test 2+; red-cell phenotype Fya+b+; eluate showed anti-Fya
Newborn serum bilirubin: 12.3 mg/dL at birth (stated normal range 2-6 mg/dL), increasing to 15.4 mg/dL after 24 hours
cases.final_diagnosis: Hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN) caused by maternal anti-Fya alloantibodies.

cases.case_summary: A 22-year-old woman presented with dull, continuous pain in the upper right rear jaw that was relieved after taking medication.
cases.full_text:
A 22-year-old woman presented with dull, continuous pain in the upper right rear jaw that was relieved after taking medication.
Night pain: History of night pain
Percussion: Symptomatic tenderness to percussion
Affected tooth: Right maxillary first premolar
Radiographic examination: Radiolucency on the distal aspect of the tooth approaching the pulp
Periodontal ligament: Widening of the periodontal ligament associated with the tooth
Electric pulp test: Delayed response
Radiographic root outline: Three outlines of roots
cases.final_diagnosis: Symptomatic irreversible pulpitis with apical periodontitis in a three-rooted maxillary first premolar, an anatomical variant resembling a small molar.

cases.case_summary: A 63-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with abdominal pain that had begun abruptly a few hours earlier and was rated ten out of ten, with nausea and one episode of vomiting.
cases.full_text:
A 63-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with abdominal pain that had begun abruptly a few hours earlier and was rated ten out of ten, with nausea and one episode of vomiting.
Preceding abdominal symptoms: Less severe postprandial abdominal pain for several months, with decreased oral intake because of fear of pain
Examination on arrival: Afebrile with stable vital signs, appearing uncomfortable with significant abdominal pain
Computed tomography in October 2017: A mass near the third portion of the duodenum and the root of the mesentery, found during evaluation of intermittent abdominal cramping and diarrhea
Biopsy of the mass: Well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor
DOTATATE PET/CT: A small bowel primary likely arising from the terminal ileum, with multiple lesions in the neck, chest, and liver
Relationship of the periduodenal mass to the mesenteric vessels: The mass intimately involved the root of the mesentery, superior mesenteric artery, and superior mesenteric vein
Computed tomography at presentation: New decreased enhancement and bowel-wall thickening of several small-bowel loops in the right lower quadrant
Exploratory laparotomy: Chylous ascites, a foreshortened mesentery adherent to a large mesenteric mass, and a 40 cm nonviable loop of intestine 10 cm from the ileocecal valve
cases.final_diagnosis: Acute-on-chronic mesenteric ischemia caused by metastatic small bowel neuroendocrine tumor with encasement of the superior mesenteric artery and vein.

cases.case_summary: A 77-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with ongoing palpitations for 3 hours and intermittent atypical chest pain over the past week.
cases.full_text:
A 77-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with ongoing palpitations for 3 hours and intermittent atypical chest pain over the past week.
Past medical history: Well-controlled arterial hypertension and dyslipidemia.
Electrocardiogram: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response.
Transthoracic echocardiography: No significant structural abnormalities, normal left ventricular function, and no valvular pathology.
Serum cardiac enzymes: Troponin and other cardiac enzymes were negative for myocardial ischemia.
CT coronary angiography calcium score: Calcium score 2 Agatston units.
CT coronary angiography: Small area of nonobstructive coronary artery disease (CAD-RADS 1) in the distal left main coronary artery.
CT coronary angiography coronary anatomy: The left main and right coronary arteries originated from a single ostium in the right sinus of Valsalva. The left main followed a long course anterior to the right ventricular outflow tract before bifurcating into the left anterior descending and left circumflex arteries. The right coronary artery had a normal anatomical course.
cases.final_diagnosis: Lipton Type RII-A single coronary artery anomaly (benign variant), with nonobstructive coronary artery disease as an incidental finding. Symptoms were attributed to atrial fibrillation rather than ischemic or structural heart disease.

cases.case_summary: A 40-year-old patient presented on July 20, 2023, with fatigue for over a month.
cases.full_text:
A 40-year-old patient presented on July 20, 2023, with fatigue for over a month.
Anticancer treatment history: Camrelizumab 200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks was started seven months before admission, with the last dose 21 days before admission. Concurrent apatinib 250 mg once daily was stopped 72 days before admission after recurrent drug-induced liver injury.
Past medical history: No history of autoimmune disease, hypertension, diabetes, heart disease, or food or drug allergy, and no recent proton pump inhibitor or NSAID use.
Serum electrolytes, creatine kinase, and urine pH: From 30 days before admission until the day before admission, serum potassium was 2.58–2.85 mmol/L, chloride 111.0–115.1 mmol/L, and carbon dioxide binding capacity 13.2–16.2 mmol/L, with a normal serum anion gap, normal creatine kinase, and urine pH 7–7.5.
Response to potassium chloride: Fatigue persisted despite intravenous and oral potassium chloride.
Arterial blood gas: Two days after admission: pH 7.34, partial pressure of carbon dioxide 23 mmHg, partial pressure of oxygen 54 mmHg, oxygen saturation 85.9%, actual bicarbonate 12.2 mmol/L, standard bicarbonate 15.4 mmol/L, and total carbon dioxide 12.9 mmol/L.
24-hour urine biochemistry: Sodium 78 mmol/L, potassium 33.96 mmol/L (reported as elevated), chloride 91.1 mmol/L, and calcium 1.85 mmol/L.
Antinuclear antibody spectrum: Strongly positive anti-SSA and anti-Ro-52 antibodies, with the remainder of the antinuclear antibody spectrum negative.
Lip gland biopsy and dryness symptoms: On the eighth day after admission, lip gland biopsy showed mild lobular atrophy and scattered lymphocyte infiltration. There were no typical symptoms of dry mouth or dry eyes.
cases.final_diagnosis: Rheumatic immune-related adverse event (irAE): Undifferentiated connective tissue disease (UCTD) associated with immune checkpoint inhibitor use, manifesting as secondary type I renal tubular acidosis (RTA) and refractory grade 3 hypokalemia.

cases.case_summary: A 47-year-old man presents with a painless, nonmobile ulcerated lesion at the left angle of the upper lip that has been present for 1 year.
cases.full_text:
A 47-year-old man presents with a painless, nonmobile ulcerated lesion at the left angle of the upper lip that has been present for 1 year.
Tobacco history: Heavy smoker
Past medical and trauma history: No significant past medical history and no history of facial trauma
Family history: No family history of cancer
Presenting lesion: Painless, nonmobile ulcerated lesion at the left angle of the upper lip for 1 year
Upper lip examination: Non-tender, non-mobile soft nodule at the left upper-lip angle; lobulated, red, irregular border, with occasional discharge
Intraoral examination: No other intraoral masses
Incisional biopsy histopathology: Dermal-based nodular tumor of basaloid-appearing cells with multivacuolated cells, moderate polymorphism, atypia, and frequent mitoses; no peripheral palisading or squamous differentiation
Immunohistochemistry: Positive for broad-spectrum cytokeratin (AE1-AE3); partial positivity for EMA; increased P53; Ki-67 about 50% in hotspot areas; negative for S100 and CEA
cases.final_diagnosis: Sebaceous carcinoma of the upper lip.

cases.case_summary: A 47-year-old man presented to the outpatient department with right-sided weakness in the upper and lower limbs for six hours, intermittent high-grade fever for four weeks, loss of appetite, and progressive weight loss.
cases.full_text:
A 47-year-old man presented to the outpatient department with right-sided weakness in the upper and lower limbs for six hours, intermittent high-grade fever for four weeks, loss of appetite, and progressive weight loss.
Past medical history: Rheumatic heart disease status post mitral valve replacement and diabetes mellitus; taking anticoagulants and oral hypoglycemic agents.
Outside hospital evaluation ten days earlier: Negative fever panel for dengue, microfilaria, microparasites, scrub typhus, and leptospirosis; blood cultures showed no growth.
Neurological examination: Right-sided paresis affecting both the upper and lower limbs; sensory, cranial nerve, and cerebellum testing normal.
Cardiovascular examination: Diastolic murmur in the aortic area and a prosthetic click in the mitral area.
Fundoscopic examination: Roth’s spots.
CT of the brain: Intraparenchymal hemorrhage in the right basifrontal lobe with surrounding edema and adjacent subarachnoid hemorrhage, a hemorrhagic focus in the posterior limb of the left internal capsule, chronic lacunar infarcts, and a subacute to chronic nonhemorrhagic infarct in the right corona radiata.
Blood cultures: Abiotrophia defectiva grew from cultures taken at three different sites.
Transesophageal echocardiogram: 9 x 9 mm vegetation on the aortic valve and bileaflet prosthetic valve, with no vegetation in the mitral valve area.
cases.final_diagnosis: Infective endocarditis caused by Abiotrophia defectiva with embolic stroke (hemorrhagic and ischemic) as a complication.

cases.case_summary: A toddler presented to the emergency department with a low-grade fever of 100°F since that morning, cough and cold symptoms for one day, and breathing difficulty that began the same morning.
cases.full_text:
A toddler presented to the emergency department with a low-grade fever of 100°F since that morning, cough and cold symptoms for one day, and breathing difficulty that began the same morning.
Growth, development, and immunizations: Thriving well, developmentally normal, and fully immunized
Gastrointestinal and urinary symptoms: No history of vomiting, loose stools, or burning during urination
General appearance on admission: Did not appear visibly ill, but had fever and rapid breathing
Cardiorespiratory examination: Pulse rate 133 per minute, respiratory rate 62 per minute, visible subcostal retractions, and wheezing in both lungs
Chest X-ray: Bilateral hyperinflated lung fields
C-reactive protein: 15.1 mg/L
Blood culture: Sterile
Nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR: Positive for human bocavirus with a cycle threshold of 28; negative for respiratory syncytial virus
cases.final_diagnosis: Human Bocavirus (HBoV) infection presenting as a wheeze-associated viral lower respiratory tract infection.

cases.case_summary: A 28-year-old primigravida at 10 weeks and one day of gestation presented with per-vaginal spotting.
cases.full_text:
A 28-year-old primigravida at 10 weeks and one day of gestation presented with per-vaginal spotting.
Menstrual history: Menarche at 13 years of age, with regular cycles and no clots or dysmenorrhea.
Intercourse symptom history: History of dyspareunia.
Conception history: Spontaneous conception after one and a half years of marriage.
Urine pregnancy test: Pregnancy confirmed by urine pregnancy test at 45 days of amenorrhea.
Associated symptoms: No lower abdominal pain, fever, foul-smelling discharge, or burning micturition.
Speculum examination: A speculum could not be inserted.
Vaginal examination: The hymen ring had a small opening, and minimal altered color blood was noted.
Ultrasound: Single intrauterine pregnancy with absent fetal cardiac activity.
cases.final_diagnosis: Microperforate hymen with concurrent missed miscarriage.

cases.case_summary: A 35-year-old man visits the dermatology clinic because of lower-extremity lesions he first noticed a month ago. The lesions are neither painful nor itchy.
cases.full_text:
A 35-year-old man visits the dermatology clinic because of lower-extremity lesions he first noticed a month ago. The lesions are neither painful nor itchy.
Medical and social history: Nonsmoker and nonalcoholic, with no chronic diseases.
Esophageal and dietary history: Esophageal irritation triggered specifically by certain foods, including citrus fruits, with dietary restrictions.
Gastroenterology evaluation: No signs of gastrointestinal disease, and no medications prescribed.
Systemic symptoms: Headaches and fever.
Lower extremity skin examination: Follicular hyperkeratosis, perifollicular bleeding, and corkscrew hairs on the lower extremities.
Oral cavity examination: Gums bleed easily after minor trauma, with multiple hematomas and hemorrhagic purpura on the palate.
Laboratory tests: Most values within normal limits; erythrocyte sedimentation rate 41 mm/hr.
Chest radiograph: No abnormalities.
cases.final_diagnosis: Scurvy caused by chronic vitamin C deficiency secondary to poor dietary intake.

cases.case_summary: A 68-year-old woman presented with fatigue, dizziness, and low blood pressure for two days, with episodes of constrictive chest pain early in the morning.
cases.full_text:
A 68-year-old woman presented with fatigue, dizziness, and low blood pressure for two days, with episodes of constrictive chest pain early in the morning.
Medical history: Prednisone 5 mg daily for p-ANCA vasculitis, stage 5 chronic kidney disease on hemodialysis three times weekly, and untreated secondary hypertension.
Admission laboratory tests: Hemoglobin 7.8 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume 99.6 fL, C-reactive protein 0.7 mg/dL, and hs-cTnI less than 50 ng/L.
Electrocardiogram: Right bundle branch block, previously known, left anterior fascicular block, inverted T waves in DIII, aVF, and V1, and a biphasic T wave in V3.
Echocardiogram: Left ventricular hypertrophy, volumetric left ventricular ejection fraction 55%, and no segmental wall-motion abnormalities.
Repeat assessment five hours after arrival: Chest pain and nausea, systolic blood pressure 70 mmHg, pulse 50 bpm, oxygen saturation 87% on room air requiring noradrenaline and oxygen, junctional escape rhythm with biphasic T waves in V1–V3, and hs-cTnI rising from 62.6 ng/L to 560 ng/L without echocardiographic changes.
Coronary angiography: 30–40% stenoses of the proximal and medial anterior descending artery and a 30% stenosis of the medial circumflex artery.
Intracoronary ergonovine test: Ergonovine 20, 30, 40, and 50 µg into the left coronary artery caused 50–60% narrowing of the proximal and medial anterior descending artery with chest pain; the narrowing and pain resolved after intracoronary nitroglycerin. The right coronary artery was not tested.
Coronary flow during provoked narrowing: Slow flow occurred with anterior descending artery narrowing described as less than 90%.
cases.final_diagnosis: Coronary involvement (coronary vasospasm and microvascular dysfunction) secondary to p-ANCA-associated vasculitis. The vasculitis-induced inflammation likely caused endothelial dysfunction and coronary spasm, presenting as MINOCA.

cases.case_summary: A 33-year-old male with no known comorbidities presented with a five-day history of fever without chills or rigors, loose stools, vomiting, and an intermittent dry cough.
cases.full_text:
A 33-year-old male with no known comorbidities presented with a five-day history of fever without chills or rigors, loose stools, vomiting, and an intermittent dry cough.
Stool and vomiting history: Four to five episodes of non-bloody, non-foul-smelling loose stools over one day, and three episodes of non-bloody, non-bilious vomiting three days prior.
Vital signs: Pulse 112 beats per minute, blood pressure 90/60 mmHg, oxygen saturation 97% on room air, respiratory rate 24 breaths per minute.
Complete blood count: Total leukocyte count 2880 cells/mm3, with 70% neutrophils and 0% eosinophils; platelet count 0.96 lakh/mm3; hemoglobin 14 g/dL.
Liver enzymes: AST 184 IU/L and ALT 72 IU/L.
Peripheral blood smear: Normal smear, with no parasites of malaria or filaria.
Dengue NS1 antigen and IgM antibody: Dengue NS1 antigen negative and dengue IgM antibodies positive.
Blood culture: Growth of S. paratyphi A.
Scrub typhus IgM and leptospirosis IgM: Scrub typhus IgM negative; leptospirosis IgM positive.
cases.final_diagnosis: Co-infections of dengue, leptospirosis, and Salmonella paratyphi A.

cases.case_summary: A 28-year-old man presented to the emergency room with acute epigastric and left hypochondrium pain for 3 days, no passage of stool or flatus over that time, and repeated non-bilious, non-projectile vomiting.
cases.full_text:
A 28-year-old man presented to the emergency room with acute epigastric and left hypochondrium pain for 3 days, no passage of stool or flatus over that time, and repeated non-bilious, non-projectile vomiting.
Prior chest injury: Road traffic accident 2 years earlier with impact over the left chest and rib fractures; a thoracostomy tube was placed, but the documents are not available.
Symptoms not reported: No abdominal distension, fever, or shortness of breath.
Respiratory rate: Tachypnea, 22 cycles per minute.
Abdominal examination: Soft, non-distended abdomen with tenderness in the left hypochondrium and epigastric region.
Chest auscultation: Breath sounds absent at the lower chest, with audible bowel sounds.
Chest radiograph: Bowel loops herniated into the left hemithorax, collapse of the lower lung zone, and no evidence of a previous fracture.
Computed tomography: Defect about 4 cm with intra-abdominal content protruding in the left hemidiaphragm, basal atelectasis of the left lung, and mild jejunal dilatation with a few air-fluid levels and no transition point.
Intraoperative inspection: 4 cm × 2 cm posterolateral left hemidiaphragm defect with protrusion of transverse colon, omentum, and part of the spleen, plus adhesions.
cases.final_diagnosis: Delayed presentation of traumatic diaphragmatic hernia secondary to a road traffic accident 2 years prior, complicated by bowel herniation through a 4 x 2 cm posterolateral diaphragmatic defect.

cases.case_summary: A 41-year-old woman presented with a 6-week history of spontaneous swelling, pain, and itching in her left breast.
cases.full_text:
A 41-year-old woman presented with a 6-week history of spontaneous swelling, pain, and itching in her left breast.
Prior breast augmentation: Bilateral textured round high profile gel breast implants, volume 535 cc, placed six years earlier in Hungary.
Breast examination: The left breast was swollen compared with the right.
Breast ultrasonography: Fluid surrounding the implant on the left side.
Breast MRI: Left peri-implant effusion without evidence of rupture, enhancement of the fibrous capsule, and lymphadenopathy in the left axilla.
Seroma fluid cytology: Foam cells and a foreign body reaction, with no evidence of malignancy.
Intraoperative frozen section: Masses excised from within the left capsule; frozen sections inconclusive.
Capsule histology: Multiple nodular distensions with aggregates of sparsely arranged blastic cells having oval, kidney-shaped nuclei, on a background of small chromatin-dense lymphocytes, plasma cells, histiocytes, and eosinophilic granulocytes.
Immunohistochemistry: Uniformly negative for ALK and CD3 and positive for CD4 and CD30.
cases.final_diagnosis: Breast Implant-Associated Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma (BIA-ALCL)

cases.case_summary: A 49-year-old woman is stable on the first day after hip surgery, when follow-up blood counts are obtained.
cases.full_text:
A 49-year-old woman is stable on the first day after hip surgery, when follow-up blood counts are obtained.
Brain magnetic resonance imaging: Three years earlier, an acute infarct in the right fronto-parietal-temporal lobe and gangliocapsular region (right middle cerebral artery territory), with non-visualization of the M2, M3, and M4 segments, possibly due to thrombosis.
History of autoimmune or renal disease: No known autoimmune disorders or renal diseases.
Preoperative blood tests: Creatinine, platelet count, and hemoglobin were normal.
Postoperative day 1 blood tests: LDH 714, platelet count 114,000, creatinine 7.4, and hemoglobin 9.7 g/dL.
Peripheral blood smear: Moderate thrombocytopenia and fragmented red blood cells.
Ultrasonography of the kidneys, ureters, and bladder: Suggested grade 1 renal parenchymal disease.
ADAMTS13 activity: Above 50%.
Shiga toxin fecal polymerase chain reaction: Negative.
cases.final_diagnosis: Atypical Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (aHUS), likely triggered by surgical stress following elective hip arthroplasty.

cases.case_summary: A 36-year-old man presented to the emergency room with intermittent, mild, dull aching right loin pain for three months, which had increased in intensity over the past day, and a mild fever for one day.
cases.full_text:
A 36-year-old man presented to the emergency room with intermittent, mild, dull aching right loin pain for three months, which had increased in intensity over the past day, and a mild fever for one day.
Gastrointestinal and urinary symptoms: No nausea, vomiting, hematuria, dysuria, or burning micturition.
Flank examination: Right renal angle tenderness.
Blood tests: Complete blood count, serum urea, creatinine, liver function, and coagulation profile were normal. ESR was 36 mm/hr.
Urine culture and acid-fast bacillus testing: Urine culture positive for Enterococcus. Urine negative for acid-fast bacillus.
Computed tomography: Large heterogeneous lesion, attenuation +20 HU, about 8.6 x 8.9 x 9.4 cm (anteroposterior x transverse x craniocaudal), arising from the inter pole region, with a few hyperdense solid components and septations, and no significant contrast enhancement.
CT-guided fine-needle aspiration: Sparsely cellular haemorrhagic smear with no atypical cells.
Operative inspection: Dense adhesions between the kidney and pararenal tissue and fat. A cyst about 9 x 10 cm arose from the posterior mid-region of the right kidney, with slough on its surface, abutting the second part of the duodenum and the lower surface of the liver. No communication with the pelvicalyceal system. The cyst contained sloughy, thick, tenacious purulent material.
Microscopic examination: Lipid-laden foamy macrophages accompanied by both chronic- and acute-phase inflammatory cells.
cases.final_diagnosis: Focal xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis (XGPN) presenting as a complex renal cyst, confirmed by histopathology.

cases.case_summary: A 46-year-old woman was referred in August 2024 for follow-up of a left breast mass that she said had been present for many years.
cases.full_text:
A 46-year-old woman was referred in August 2024 for follow-up of a left breast mass that she said had been present for many years.
Left breast physical examination: Painless, soft, mobile, palpable mass in the outer (lateral) left breast
Mammography: Oval, circumscribed, predominantly fatty mass measuring about 9.5 × 7.5 × 8 cm in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast
Mammography of the internal lesion: Hyperdense mass measuring approximately 4.5 × 4 × 3 cm, with an irregular shape, spiculated margins, and coarse heterogeneous microcalcifications within the fatty mass
Breast magnetic resonance imaging: Oval, circumscribed mass of predominant internal adipose intensity without enhancement, containing an internal irregular spiculated mass with heterogeneous T2 hypointensity, heterogeneous enhancement, and medium/plateau kinetics
Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy of the irregular mass: Benign tissue composed of ducts, lobules, and adipose tissue in a disorganized structure
Gross examination of the excised mass: Well-circumscribed tumor composed of randomly arranged, well-differentiated glandular and stromal mammary structures, adipose tissue, and smooth muscle
Microscopic examination of the excised mass: Lobules, ducts, fibrous stroma, and adipose tissue arranged in a disorganized structure
Histologic evaluation of glands, atypia, and mitosis: Normal glands and lobules, with no cytoarchitectural atypia and no significant mitosis
cases.final_diagnosis: Breast hamartoma with internal benign pathology, despite radiologic features suspicious for malignancy

cases.case_summary: A 47-year-old man presented to a local clinic with palpitation.
cases.full_text:
A 47-year-old man presented to a local clinic with palpitation.
Presenting complaint: Palpitation
12-lead electrocardiogram: Third-degree atrioventricular block
Transthoracic echocardiography: Normal ventricular and valve function, with a well-demarcated hypoechoic ovoid mass measuring 29.9 mm × 25.6 mm in the interatrial septum
Transesophageal echocardiography with color Doppler: Large, homogeneous, hypoechoic mass with no stalk and no color flow signal within the mass
Myocardial contrast echocardiography: Hypoechogenic atrial septal mass with clear, regular boundaries and no obvious contrast agent perfusion
Computed tomography coronary angiography: No obvious stenosis in the left main, anterior descending, circumflex, or right coronary arteries. Low-density ovoid atrial septal mass with well-defined borders, no significant enhancement, and no feeding vessels from the coronary arteries
Magnetic resonance imaging: No fat deposition and no late gadolinium enhancement
Gross and histologic examination of the resected mass: Cyst containing muddy, milky mucous liquid; wall composed of stratified ciliated columnar epithelium with smooth muscle cells
cases.final_diagnosis: Bronchogenic cyst in the interatrial septum

cases.case_summary: A 47-year-old woman had intermittent low back pain for more than three months and was admitted to the hospital on May 21, 2020.
cases.full_text:
A 47-year-old woman had intermittent low back pain for more than three months and was admitted to the hospital on May 21, 2020.
Low back pain: Intermittent low back pain for more than three months
Chest CT: Low-density mass at the left anterior edge of the T4-5 vertebral body in the posterior mediastinum, with a clear boundary and a CT value of about 20 Hu
Contrast-enhanced chest CT: No obvious enhancement
Chest MRI: Cystic-shaped lesion in the left posterior mediastinum with long T1 and long T2 signal, a clear boundary, and a size of approximately 1.8 cm × 2.0 cm × 3.8 cm
Immunohistochemistry of the lining epithelium: Diffuse expression of estrogen receptor (ER), PAX8, WT1, and protein kinase C (PKC); negative for calretinin; low Ki-67 proliferation
cases.final_diagnosis: Posterior mediastinal Mullerian cyst

cases.case_summary: A 58-year-old woman developed diffuse erythematous edema and infiltrations of the face, with nodular lesions on the nose, the left ear, and both nipples.
cases.full_text:
A 58-year-old woman developed diffuse erythematous edema and infiltrations of the face, with nodular lesions on the nose, the left ear, and both nipples.
Hematologic history: Known chronic lymphatic B-cell leukemia in stable disease for five years.
Prior Lyme borreliosis diagnosis and treatment: No previous diagnosis or treatment for Lyme borreliosis.
Skin examination: Diffuse erythematous edema and infiltrations of the face, with nodular lesions on the nose, left ear, and both nipples.
Immunohistochemistry of skin lymphocytic infiltrates: Positive for CD20, CD3, CD79a, and CD25; negative for CD5 and myeloperoxidase.
Bone marrow immunohistology: 60% infiltration by neoplastic cells expressing CD20, CD5, and CD23, with a proliferation rate of 10%.
Borrelia ELISA: High concentrations of anti-borrelial IgG antibodies.
Borrelia immunoblot: A broad spectrum of B. burgdorferi-specific bands was visible.
PCR and culture of skin biopsies: B. burgdorferi DNA detected by PCR in the affected lesions; B. burgdorferi sensu stricto cultured from the left ear and the right mammilla.
cases.final_diagnosis: Disseminated borrelial lymphocytoma associated with Borrelia burgdorferi sensu stricto infection in a patient with underlying chronic lymphatic leukemia (B-CLL)

cases.case_summary: A newborn is admitted at 9 hours and 18 minutes of age after the parents noticed yellowing of the face and skin over the previous 4 hours.
cases.full_text:
A newborn is admitted at 9 hours and 18 minutes of age after the parents noticed yellowing of the face and skin over the previous 4 hours.
Perinatal history: G3P2, born at 38+6 weeks after an uneventful delivery, with birth weight 2,600 g and Apgar scores of 10 at 1, 5, and 10 minutes. No intrauterine distress, premature rupture of membranes, or cord around the neck; amniotic fluid clear and bright, 350 ml.
Admission bilirubin: Total bilirubin 271 μmol/L and indirect bilirubin 256.9 μmol/L.
Symptoms at admission: No lethargy, agitation, crying, convulsions, reduced feeding, or decreased activity. Urine and feces were passed normally, with no abnormal appearance.
Physical examination: Temperature 36.5°C, pulse 134 beats/min, respirations 50 breaths/min, blood pressure 73/22 mmHg, and weight 2.58 kg. Yellowing of the face, neck, and trunk; liver and spleen not enlarged; heart, lung, abdominal, and neurologic examinations unremarkable; urine and feces normal in color.
Hemolysis and metabolic studies: Direct and indirect anti-human globulin tests, blood group antibody screen, hemoglobin electrophoresis, G6PD test, H inclusion bodies, and blood and urine genetic metabolism screens were negative. The pyruvate kinase test was not performed because equipment was unavailable.
Hemoglobin and bilirubin after admission: Hemoglobin fell from 142 g/L to 112 g/L, and total bilirubin rose from 271 μmol/L to 310.8 μmol/L.
Early erythrocyte microscopy: No specific erythrocyte morphologic or structural abnormalities were detected.
Whole exome sequencing: Heterozygous SPTA1 mutation c.82C>T at chr1:158655080, of paternal origin.
cases.final_diagnosis: Hereditary elliptocytosis due to a heterozygous SPTA1 gene mutation (c.82C>T)

cases.case_summary: A 37-year-old woman presents at 13 weeks and 5 days of gestation for non-invasive prenatal testing.
cases.full_text:
A 37-year-old woman presents at 13 weeks and 5 days of gestation for non-invasive prenatal testing.
Maternal and paternal karyotypes: Maternal karyotype 46,XX,t(9;18)(q34;q11.2); paternal karyotype normal
Prior pregnancy outcomes: First pregnancy ended by IVG for an unbalanced t(9;18); second pregnancy miscarried; one healthy child carries a balanced t(9;18) matching the maternal translocation
First-trimester ultrasound: Normal findings at 12 + 4 weeks, with nuchal translucency 1.9 mm
Cell-free DNA prenatal screen: High risk for dup(18)(p11.32q11.2), fetal fraction 7%
QF-PCR aneuploidy testing of amniocytes: Partial trisomy of the short arm of chromosome 18 on a panel for trisomies 13, 18, and 21 and sex-chromosome aneuploidy
G-banded karyotype of cultured amniocytes: 48,XX,+2mar in 50 metaphases
SNP array of uncultured amniocytes: 15.3 Mb four-copy gain at 18p11.32-p11.21 (12,842-15,303,932) and 926 kbp three-copy gain at 9q34.3 (140,118,286-141,044,489)
FISH with a 9q34.3 probe on amniocyte metaphases: A third signal on one of the two marker chromosomes
cases.final_diagnosis: Inherited unbalanced reciprocal translocation resulting in tetrasomy 18p (18p11.32-p11.21) and trisomy 9q (9q34.3)

cases.case_summary: A 79-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with a four-day history of sudden shortness of breath and dull, non-radiating, generalized chest pressure.
cases.full_text:
A 79-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with a four-day history of sudden shortness of breath and dull, non-radiating, generalized chest pressure.
Hematologic history: Chronic myeloid leukemia diagnosed in 2023 and under current dasatinib therapy.
Other medical history: Breast cancer treated with lumpectomy and radiation, asthma, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
Physical examination: Decreased breath sounds in both lower lobes and sinus tachycardia; the remainder of the examination was unremarkable.
CT angiogram of the chest: Moderate bilateral pleural effusions with atelectasis of both lower lobes, no pulmonary embolism, and multiple small calcified granulomas bilaterally.
Thoracentesis: 1450 mL of pleural fluid collected from the right lower lobe and 1100 mL from the left lower lobe.
Pleural fluid culture and staining: No growth at two days, a predominance of lymphocytes without organisms, and no fungal elements on calcofluor staining.
Pleural fluid analysis: Exudative effusion with elevated white blood cells, lymphocyte predominance, and elevated triglycerides.
Evaluation for other causes: No trauma, lung malignancy, or congenital anomaly was detected.
cases.final_diagnosis: Dasatinib-induced bilateral chylothorax

cases.case_summary: A five-month-old infant presents with jaundice, developmental delay, and hepatosplenomegaly.
cases.full_text:
A five-month-old infant presents with jaundice, developmental delay, and hepatosplenomegaly.
Family history: Firstborn of third-degree consanguineous parents
Neonatal history: Neonatal intensive care unit admission for four days because of neonatal hyperbilirubinemia
Abdominal examination: Liver palpable 3 cm below the right costal margin; spleen palpable 6 to 7 cm below the left costal margin, near the umbilicus
Complete blood count: Normal
Liver function tests: Deranged
Cytomegalovirus and rubella testing: Nonreactive
Portal Doppler ultrasound: Enlarged right lobe of the liver measuring 7.2 cm and enlarged spleen measuring 10.1 cm x 6.3 cm x 3.1 cm
Whole exome sequencing: Suggests a mutation in the NPC2 gene, described as exon 2-4 location of chromosome 14:g.deletion
cases.final_diagnosis: Niemann-Pick disease type C2

cases.case_summary: A 22-year-old man presents with pain and swelling in the right lower eyelid for the past two weeks.
cases.full_text:
A 22-year-old man presents with pain and swelling in the right lower eyelid for the past two weeks.
Prior orbital trauma and surgery: Road traffic accident two years earlier with a fronto-naso-orbito-ethmoidal fracture treated by open reduction and internal fixation, orbital exploration, and orbital floor reconstruction
Treatment earlier in this episode: Analgesics, antibiotic eye drops, and oral antibiotics prescribed at multiple hospitals, after which symptoms rapidly worsened
Eyelid inspection: Solitary 6 cm x 4 cm swelling of the right lower eyelid; an erythematic, voluminous mass just inferior to the medial canthus, covering most of the eye and obstructing vision
Palpation and expression of the swelling: Tender, fluctuant, and warm, with a skin fistula and punctal leakage of purulent discharge when pressure was applied
Recent trauma, fever, conjunctivitis, vision, and eye movements: No recent trauma, fever, or conjunctivitis; vision normal; extraocular movements free and full
Pus culture: Sterile
High-resolution computed tomography: Medial impingement of the orbital mesh over the nasolacrimal duct apparatus, with obvious obliteration
Orbital exploration: Medial mesh flange overextended and fused to the medial nasal bone, compromising nasolacrimal duct patency
cases.final_diagnosis: Dacryocystitis secondary to obstruction caused by migrated orbital mesh implant following a previous orbital floor fracture repair.

cases.case_summary: A 61-year-old male truck driver was found in cardiopulmonary arrest on his cab seat about 30 minutes after he complained of chest pain at the office. He had a history of hypertension. Emergency physicians performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation, but he was pronounced dead.
cases.full_text:
A 61-year-old male truck driver was found in cardiopulmonary arrest on his cab seat about 30 minutes after he complained of chest pain at the office. He had a history of hypertension. Emergency physicians performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation, but he was pronounced dead.
Past medical history: History of hypertension.
Circumstances of collapse: Found in cardiopulmonary arrest on a driver's cab seat approximately 30 minutes after complaining of chest pain at the office.
Perivascular fat attenuation index: −57 HU in the RCA, −73 HU in the LAD, and −64 HU in the LCX.
Coronary arteries at autopsy: Right-dominant coronary artery with around 90% luminal stenosis about 4.0 cm distal to the RCA origin, around 70% luminal stenosis about 3.0 cm distal to the LCX origin, and no significant luminal stenosis in the LAD.
Myocardium from the ventricular septum to the posterior left ventricular wall: Contractile zone necrosis, myocardial tears, and myocardial wave-like running, reported as mild changes suggestive of acute myocardial ischemia.
Anterior to lateral myocardial wall: Whitish discoloration approximately 1.5 × 1.5 cm, with fibrosis and no inflammatory cell infiltration on histology.
Other organs: No obvious lesions on macroscopic observation or histological examination.
cases.final_diagnosis: Ischemic heart failure due to acute myocardial ischemia originating from significant RCA atherosclerotic stenosis

cases.case_summary: A 23-year-old man presented to the outpatient department with an asymptomatic lesion on the deltoid region of his right arm that had been present for eight years.
cases.full_text:
A 23-year-old man presented to the outpatient department with an asymptomatic lesion on the deltoid region of his right arm that had been present for eight years.
History of the lesion course: Spontaneous resolution, with reappearance after two to three months of resolution.
History of change in the lesion: No progression in dimension, structure, or color.
History of lesions elsewhere: No similar lesions on any other body part.
History of local symptoms: No pain, itching, or tenderness on or around the lesion.
Inspection of the lesion: Blue-black lesion surrounded by a red ecchymotic ring.
Lesion measurement: 2x1 cm.
Dermoscopy: Central blue-black area surrounded and demarcated by a red homogenous area with vascular structures; the central lesion is margined by red borders through its circumference.
Histopathologic examination: Dilated blood vessels lined by hobnail epithelial cells, with hemosiderin depositions in the deeper dermis.
cases.final_diagnosis: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma (THH)

cases.case_summary: A 17-year-old male presents with progressive pain and swelling of the right knee, with functional impairment and ipsilateral muscular atrophy.
cases.full_text:
A 17-year-old male presents with progressive pain and swelling of the right knee, with functional impairment and ipsilateral muscular atrophy.
Right ankle history: Eleven years earlier, synovial haemangioma of the right ankle was diagnosed and confirmed by excisional biopsy.
Trauma history: No significant trauma reported.
Knee radiograph: Diminished bone mineralization, epiphysial overgrowth, and intercondylar groove widening, with femorotibial subchondral sclerosis and joint space reduction.
Knee MRI: Multiple lobulated nodular coalescent lesions within the knee joint space, infiltrating the suprapatellar fat pad and Hoffa’s fat pad.
MRI signal and enhancement: Lesions were hyperintense on proton-density fat-saturated images and intermediate signal on T1-weighted images, with significant gadolinium enhancement and vascular supply from popliteal arterial branches.
Excisional biopsy histopathology: Spindle cell haemangioma in the seven excised nodules.
cases.final_diagnosis: intermediate-type synovial hemangioma of the right knee

cases.case_summary: A 55-year-old woman presented with pain and discomfort in the right knee.
cases.full_text:
A 55-year-old woman presented with pain and discomfort in the right knee.
Earlier right knee pain: Falls four years earlier were followed by insidious-onset, gradually progressive, continuous, sharp, nonradiating right knee pain.
Recent pain and function: Pain had aggravated over the last year, and she had difficulty climbing stairs.
Medial joint-line palpation: Tenderness over the right medial joint line.
Knee motion and valgus stress: Range of motion of the right and left knees was 0 to 120 degrees, and the right knee showed valgus stress.
Plain radiographs: Anteroposterior and lateral radiographs showed an intra-articular loose body.
MRI: Intra-articular mass in the intercondylar notch, hyperintense to muscle.
Arthroscopy: Medial meniscus degenerative tear and a floating loose body about 2 cm × 2 cm, with no evidence of connectivity with bone.
Microscopic examination: Mature bony trabeculae enclosing fatty marrow spaces, encapsulated by a hyaline cartilaginous membrane, with no mitotic figures or chondrocyte atypia.
cases.final_diagnosis: A solitary intra-articular osteochondroma in the right knee, presenting as a loose body associated with a medial meniscus degenerative tear.

cases.case_summary: On day two of life, a dried blood spot collected for newborn screening was flagged for hyperphenylalaninemia.
cases.full_text:
On day two of life, a dried blood spot collected for newborn screening was flagged for hyperphenylalaninemia.
Birth and family history: Boy born at term by normal vaginal delivery to non-consanguineous parents, mother of Chinese descent and father Spanish, with an uneventful perinatal history and an unremarkable family history.
Newborn screening phenylalanine: Dried blood spot phenylalanine 233 μmol/L (reference range 34–84 μmol/L), with a phenylalanine-to-tyrosine ratio of 2.38 (reference range 0.27–1.1), on day two of life.
Day 12 phenylalanine: Dried blood spot phenylalanine 236 μmol/L (reference range 24–70 μmol/L) and plasma phenylalanine 272 μmol/L (reference range 49–107 μmol/L).
Urine pterins: No neopterin or biopterin elevations by liquid chromatography with tandem mass spectrometry.
PAH gene Sanger sequencing: No clinically significant variants detected in the PAH gene.
DHPR activity: 2.4 mU/mg Hb at three months of age (reference normal >1.1).
Cerebrospinal fluid neurotransmitter metabolites and phenylalanine: At three months, CSF HVA 248 nmol/L (reference range 295–932 nmol/L), 5-HIAA 75 nmol/L (reference range 114–336 nmol/L), and CSF phenylalanine 42 μmol/L (reference range 5–21 μmol/L).
DNAJC12 gene sequencing and parental genotyping: Compound heterozygous NM_021800.3: c.214C>T p.(Arg72*) and NM_021800.3: c.185C>A p.(Ala62Glu); the nonsense variant was inherited from the father and the missense variant from the mother.
cases.final_diagnosis: DNAJC12 deficiency

cases.case_summary: In June 2020, a patient is admitted to the emergency department with hemoptysis and chest pain.
cases.full_text:
In June 2020, a patient is admitted to the emergency department with hemoptysis and chest pain.
Earlier cough and hemoptysis: Symptoms began in November 2019 without an obvious cause: cough with a small amount of white mucus, no fever, wheezing, or cyanosis, and nighttime hemoptysis of approximately 10 mL of bright red sputum.
Peripheral blood eosinophil count: Eosinophil count 0.07 × 109/L (normal range 0.02–0.52 × 109/L), eosinophil percentage 0.5% (normal range 0.4–8.0%).
Tuberculosis tests: T-SPOT.TB and tuberculosis smear tests were negative.
Chest CT: Bilateral lower-lung cord-like opacities and nodular shadows involving the right upper lung and both lower lungs, with a small lesion. Strip-like shadows connected lesions in the ipsilateral lung.
Emergency chest CT: Small bilateral pneumothorax and extensive neck and mediastinal pneumatization. Multiple thin-walled cavities surrounded by non-uniform hazy rims in both lungs, most connected through a tunnel structure.
Serum multiple-dot ELISA for helminth antibodies: Positive for Sparganum.
Lung biopsy histopathology: Alveolar epithelial hyperplasia, foam cell aggregation in the alveolar lumen, iron-containing hematoxylin deposition, and a small amount of eosinophilic infiltration.
Freshwater exposure: He had swum in a local reservoir and accidentally ingested water from the reservoir 3 months before symptom onset.
cases.final_diagnosis: pulmonary sparganosis

cases.case_summary: A 63-year-old man presented with fever on and off for 15 days and a dry cough with dyspnea on exertion for seven days.
cases.full_text:
A 63-year-old man presented with fever on and off for 15 days and a dry cough with dyspnea on exertion for seven days.
Appetite and weight: Loss of appetite and weight loss of 5-6 kg over two months
Pleural effusion history: Known bilateral recurrent pleural effusion
Associated history: No chest pain, hemoptysis, pleural tuberculosis, or comorbidities
Physical examination: Pallor, clubbing, tachypnea, hypoxia, and bilaterally reduced breath sounds
Lymph node examination: Multiple palpable lymph nodes, predominantly left posterior auricular, left posterior cervical, and right occipital
Chest radiograph and pleural drainage: Bilateral pleural effusion, right greater than left; 1500 ml drained
Sputum and pleural fluid studies: AFB test and Trunet assay of sputum and pleural fluid negative; pleural fluid suggested an exudative effusion with low ADA by Light criteria
Lymph node biopsy: Follicular lymphoid hyperplasia with focal, circumscribed paracortical necrotizing lesions, abundant karyorrhectic debris, and a collection of large mononuclear cells
cases.final_diagnosis: Kikuchi-Fujimoto Disease (KFD)

cases.case_summary: A 48-year-old man presented with jaundice and abdominal pain that had lasted one year.
cases.full_text:
A 48-year-old man presented with jaundice and abdominal pain that had lasted one year.
Abdominal pain and associated symptoms: Dull, non-radiating pain in both the right and left hypochondriac regions, with vomiting and loose stools, for the past year
Prior discoloration of eyes and nails: Recurrent yellowish discoloration of the eyes and nails
Family history of genetic disorders: No family history of genetic disorders
Abdominal ultrasound: Cholecystolithiasis, gallbladder sludge, and moderate splenomegaly, with normal liver size, shape, and echo pattern and a normal portal vein
Physical examination: Yellowish discoloration of the sclera and skin; no pallor, cyanosis, clubbing, or lymphadenopathy; mild tenderness in the left hypochondrial region and an enlarged spleen
Coagulation studies and serum albumin: INR 0.90, prothrombin time 12.24 seconds, and serum albumin 4.4 g/dL
Serum total bilirubin: Total bilirubin 19.58 mg/dL, with no anemia
Eosin-5'-maleimide binding flow cytometry: 19.5% reduction in mean fluorescence intensity
cases.final_diagnosis: Hereditary spherocytosis

cases.case_summary: In 2021, a 53-year-old man presented for a routine postoperative check.
cases.full_text:
In 2021, a 53-year-old man presented for a routine postoperative check.
Reason for seeking care: Mild chest discomfort in 2019
Cardiac auscultation: Grade 4/6 systolic ejection murmur in the third and fourth left intercostal spaces
Electrocardiogram: Inverted T-waves and abnormal QRS complexes in nearly all leads
Transthoracic echocardiography: Diastolic interventricular septal thickness 27 mm, maximum basal thickness 30 mm, diastolic left ventricular posterior wall thickness 24 mm, systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve, and resting left ventricular outflow tract gradient 109 mmHg
Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging: Late gadolinium enhancement showed diffuse left ventricular fibrosis, without reduction of T1 mapping
GLA sequencing: c.595T>C (p.Val199Met) in exon 4 of GLA, confirmed by Sanger sequencing
Plasma α-galactosidase A activity: 0.43 μmol/L/h (reference range 2.40–17.65 μmol/L/h)
Plasma globotriaosylsphingosine: 12.30 ng/ml (reference range < 1.1 ng/ml)
cases.final_diagnosis: Fabry disease

cases.case_summary: In October 2022, during the late stages of orthodontic treatment, the patient reported pain and mobility of the upper left first premolar.
cases.full_text:
In October 2022, during the late stages of orthodontic treatment, the patient reported pain and mobility of the upper left first premolar.
Medical history: Type 1 diabetes
Upper-arch bracket placement: In March 2021, brackets were bonded to the upper teeth except the two left premolars, which were in good occlusion
Earlier status of the upper left first premolar: Good relationship with the opposing tooth and no clinical signs during treatment
Symptoms: Pain and mobility of the upper left first premolar
Orthodontic appliance coverage: The upper left first premolar was not included in the orthodontic appliance
Dental operating microscope examination: Mesio-distal crack extending occlusogingivally into the root
cases.final_diagnosis: Crack tooth syndrome in the upper left first premolar

cases.case_summary: A 56-year-old woman developed a fever of 38.1 °C about two days after consolidation chemotherapy, once medullar aplasia with severe pancytopenia had been attained.
cases.full_text:
A 56-year-old woman developed a fever of 38.1 °C about two days after consolidation chemotherapy, once medullar aplasia with severe pancytopenia had been attained.
Hematologic diagnosis: Acute myeloid leukemia, FLT3-positive
Clinical status: Medullar aplasia with severe pancytopenia after consolidation chemotherapy, then fever of 38.1 °C about 2 days later
Initial blood cultures: No specific pathogen isolated
Fever during empiric antibiotics: Fever persisted while receiving piperacillin-tazobactam and vancomycin
Repeat blood cultures: Bacterial growth in both sets after 5 days of incubation in a BD BACTEC FX40 system, noted as possibly indicating a low bacterial concentration
Central venous catheter culture: No growth from the removed central venous catheter
Gram stain of the blood-culture isolate: Gram-positive cocci in chains or pairs
Blood culture identification: Leuconostoc pseudomesenteroides
cases.final_diagnosis: Leuconostoc pseudomesenteroides bacteremia

cases.case_summary: A six-year-old boy is brought to the children’s emergency department with sudden weight loss, fatigue, night sweats, and decreased oral intake.
cases.full_text:
A six-year-old boy is brought to the children’s emergency department with sudden weight loss, fatigue, night sweats, and decreased oral intake.
Past medical history: Congenital hypothyroidism, autism, and asthma.
Levothyroxine dose: Decreased from 88 mcg to 44 mcg daily when symptoms first started, six months before presentation.
Oral intake and weight: Gradual decline in oral intake over the prior six months, with appetite sharply worse in the preceding month and inability to tolerate oral intake; weight loss of 13.6 kilograms, including 9.1 kilograms in the last month.
Initial vital signs: Blood pressure 240/168 mmHg, heart rate 133 beats per minute, temperature 36.6 °C, and a normal respiratory pattern.
Thyroid function tests: TSH 4.03 μIU/mL, described as mildly elevated; free T4 1.50 ng/dL; T3 4.13 pg/mL.
Plasma free normetanephrine and catecholamines: Plasma free normetanephrine 15.90 nmol/L; norepinephrine 13,002 pg/mL; dopamine 88 pg/mL; all reported as elevated.
Abdominal ultrasound: 5.3 x 3.3 x 4.0 cm suprarenal mass on the right kidney and a suspected enlarged periportal lymph node.
Abdominal MRI with and without contrast: Complex lobular right adrenal mass with peripheral enhancement.
cases.final_diagnosis: Pheochromocytoma of the right adrenal gland

cases.case_summary: A 24-year-old woman, gravida 2, parity 1, with a previous cesarean, presented with pain over the prior suture site.
cases.full_text:
A 24-year-old woman, gravida 2, parity 1, with a previous cesarean, presented with pain over the prior suture site.
Past obstetric history: Cesarean section two years earlier for breech presentation with premature rupture of membranes; live male infant weighing 2.7 kg.
Presenting complaint: Pain over the previous suture site.
Abdominal examination: Uterus at term, with breech presentation at the lower pole.
Scar and fetal heart rate: Suprapubic transverse scar tender to examination; fetal heart rate 140 beats/minute.
Intraoperative uterine inspection: Septum measuring about 1 cm, with two uterine cavities.
Intraoperative adnexal inspection: Both ovaries and both fallopian tubes appeared normal.
cases.final_diagnosis: Partial septate uterus

cases.case_summary: A 55-year-old man presented with progressive right shoulder pain for one month. The pain was insidious, rapidly intensifying, throbbing, and burning, did not radiate, and worsened with shoulder movement. One week before admission, he developed a low-grade continuous fever and jaundice.
cases.full_text:
A 55-year-old man presented with progressive right shoulder pain for one month. The pain was insidious, rapidly intensifying, throbbing, and burning, did not radiate, and worsened with shoulder movement. One week before admission, he developed a low-grade continuous fever and jaundice.
Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Right shoulder pain: Progressive pain for one month, insidious, rapidly intensifying, throbbing and burning, nonradiating, and worse with shoulder movement
Fever and jaundice: Low-grade continuous fever and jaundice beginning one week before admission
Physical examination: Thin, febrile, dehydrated, hypotensive, and pale; diffuse right shoulder swelling, anterior redness, warmth, tenderness, and painful movements
Hemoglobin, white blood cell count, and C-reactive protein: Hemoglobin 4.9 g/dL, white blood cell count 19,400, C-reactive protein >192 mg/L
Random blood glucose and hemoglobin A1c: Random blood sugar 233 mg/dL and hemoglobin A1c 9.1%
Magnetic resonance imaging of the right shoulder: Pus collection in the joint space and surroundings
Pus and blood culture identification: B. pseudomallei in pus and blood samples
cases.final_diagnosis: Shoulder septic arthritis caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, leading to melioidosis, in a patient with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus.

cases.case_summary: A 66-year-old man presented to the emergency department with shortness of breath, cough, and wheezing.
cases.full_text:
A 66-year-old man presented to the emergency department with shortness of breath, cough, and wheezing.
Past medical history: GERD and stage III laryngeal carcinoma status post chemotherapy, in remission.
Recent upper endoscopy: Symptoms began three days earlier, following upper endoscopy for an esophageal stricture at the cricopharyngeus muscle with a botulinum injection of 100 units.
Symptom course: Worsening dysphonia, shortness of breath, and difficulty swallowing over three days.
Respiratory examination: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, loud inspiratory stridor, and difficulty protecting the airway.
Temperature and oxygenation: Afebrile, with SpO2 90% on 2 L of O2.
Fiberoptic laryngoscopy: Diffuse laryngeal edema and erythema; both true vocal cords rested in the median position and did not move with inhalation or phonation.
cases.final_diagnosis: Bilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve paralysis secondary to botulinum toxin injection at the cricopharyngeus muscle

cases.case_summary: A 63-year-old woman with mild hypertension developed severe pain in the proximal and intermediate third of her right arm about 21 days after a dengue virus infection. The arm was atrophied, with skin color changes consistent with livedo. The pain was stabbing, shock-like, and burning, and it became unbearable.
cases.full_text:
A 63-year-old woman with mild hypertension developed severe pain in the proximal and intermediate third of her right arm about 21 days after a dengue virus infection. The arm was atrophied, with skin color changes consistent with livedo. The pain was stabbing, shock-like, and burning, and it became unbearable.
Preceding infection: Dengue virus infection about 21 days before the arm symptoms.
Right upper-limb motor examination: Amyotrophy and hypotonia in the proximal and intermediate right upper limb, with grade 2/3 paresis of the deltoid, infraspinatus, biceps brachii, brachioradialis, and triceps brachii.
Sensory examination: Allodynia to touch and pressure, thermal hyperesthesia, and hypoesthesia of deep sensation.
Deep tendon reflexes: Biceps, triceps, and brachioradialis reflexes absent on the right.
Cranial nerve examination: Cranial nerves normal.
Inflammatory, infectious, and immune laboratory screen: Results normal except for positive dengue virus IgM.
Electroneuromyography: Prolonged action potentials and latency, with acute denervation of peripheral nerves.
Brachial plexus MRI: Slight signal alterations in the upper and middle primary trunks.
cases.final_diagnosis: Post-Dengue Parsonage-Turner Syndrome (PTS)

cases.case_summary: A 15-year-old boy presents with a high-grade fever lasting one week that responds to medication. He is malnourished, and examination shows an S-shaped lateral curve of the spine, a prominent high-riding left scapula, impaired muscle control on the left, an uneven waistline, and a tuft of hair over the lumbar region.
cases.full_text:
A 15-year-old boy presents with a high-grade fever lasting one week that responds to medication. He is malnourished, and examination shows an S-shaped lateral curve of the spine, a prominent high-riding left scapula, impaired muscle control on the left, an uneven waistline, and a tuft of hair over the lumbar region.
Birth and developmental history: First-born male, born preterm at 36 weeks of gestation, with a five-day NICU admission after birth. Intellectual functioning below average for his age.
Musculoskeletal and skin examination: Pronounced S-shaped lateral curvature of the spine, scapular asymmetry with a visually prominent high-riding left scapula, impaired muscle control on the left side of the body, an uneven waistline, and a tuft of hair in the lumbar region.
Chest radiography: Dorsal spinal curvature convex toward the right from D2 to D9 and lumbar curvature convex toward the left from D12 to L5. The left scapula is elevated and rotated, with the inferior angle directed laterally, and no omovertebral bar.
CT and MRI of the ribs and vertebrae: Bilateral cervical ribs, aplasia of the left second rib, partial block vertebra from D1-D2 to D3-D4, L1-L2, and L5-S1, and dorsolumbar butterfly vertebra from D4 to L2.
CT of the lumbosacral posterior elements: Defect in the posterior elements of L2-L4, involving the spinous process.
MRI and CT of the spinal cord and dural sac: Two hemicords with a bony septum between them, a duplicated dural sac from D11-D12 to L2-L3, and an osseous septum at L1-L2.
Spine MRI: Low-lying tethered cord and a syrinx/hydromyelia.
CT and MRI of the sacrum: Partial unilateral left sacral agenesis at S1, S2, and S3.
cases.final_diagnosis: closed spinal dysraphism with scoliosis, Sprengel's deformity, diastematomyelia (type I), spina bifida occulta, tethered cord syndrome, butterfly vertebrae, block vertebrae, sacral agenesis, and associated congenital anomalies

cases.case_summary: A 47-year-old man presents with abdominal pain and a suspicious history of hematemesis.
cases.full_text:
A 47-year-old man presents with abdominal pain and a suspicious history of hematemesis.
Symptoms on arrival: Generalized abdominal pain, pallor, and a suspicious history of hematemesis and melena.
Prior arterial bypass: Two years earlier, a bifurcated graft was used for bypass from the aorta to the right common iliac artery and the left common femoral artery.
Endovascular procedure after bypass: One month after the bypass, a stent graft was placed at the right graft limb–iliac artery anastomosis because of a para-anastomotic pseudoaneurysm.
Right lower-limb course: Three months later, acute right lower-limb ischemia followed thrombosis of the right graft limb, and the right leg was amputated below the knee.
Laboratory studies: RBC 1.77×10^6/ml, hemoglobin 3 g/dl, WBC 9.1×10^3/uL with 84% neutrophils, platelets 596×10^3/uL, BUN 25 mg/dl, and creatinine 1.7 mg/dl.
Intravenous contrast CT: The right iliac artery stent is thrombosed and contains air bubbles, with circumferential graft wall thickening and ectopic gas.
CT of the right psoas muscle: The right psoas muscle is heterogeneously enlarged and contains a fluid- and air-filled collection measuring 67 × 40 × 37 mm.
Reformatted CT of the graft and adjacent bowel: A tubular fluid-filled structure beside the right iliac graft corresponds to the third part of the duodenum, which is mildly irregular and thickened, with loss of the fat plane against the thrombosed graft.
cases.final_diagnosis: Secondary iliac graft-enteric fistula

cases.case_summary: A 9-year-old boy is brought by his mother to the pediatric clinic because of difficulty standing, walking, and running with his classmates.
cases.full_text:
A 9-year-old boy is brought by his mother to the pediatric clinic because of difficulty standing, walking, and running with his classmates.
Early motor development: No neonatal hypotonia. Neck support at about 5 months and independent walking at about 19 months.
Motor symptom history: At age 4, easy fatigue during play and repeated falls. At age 6, difficulty standing, walking, and running; he climbed stairs alone with slight difficulty and got up from the floor using his arms. He lagged behind peers in school competitions.
Family history: Parents are first-degree cousins and have four sons. The two oldest sons were asymptomatic. The youngest had a limping gait, difficulty bending his right knee, muscle pain, and fatigability.
Lower-limb strength examination: Proximal lower-limb muscles mildly weak, mainly the hip extensors, at MRC grade 4/5, with no muscular atrophy.
Ankle examination and Gowers sign: Slight left ankle contracture affecting dorsiflexion. Gowers sign positive.
Distal lower-limb and upper-limb examination: Distal lower-limb muscles, both upper limbs, and the shoulder muscles had normal power and shape.
Serum creatine kinase: 335 U/L (reference range 39–308 U/L).
Whole-exome sequencing: Homozygous NM_001849.4: c.1817-3C>G in COL6A2; his symptomatic brother was also homozygous.
cases.final_diagnosis: Bethlem myopathy caused by a homozygous COL6A2 splice site variant (c.1817-3C>G)

cases.case_summary: A 57-year-old male presented with itchy erythematous skin lesions over his right ankle for 20 days.
cases.full_text:
A 57-year-old male presented with itchy erythematous skin lesions over his right ankle for 20 days.
Topical treatment and lesion course: Over-the-counter topical steroid was applied from the day after onset until presentation. Erythema initially seemed reduced; after five days the lesions aggravated, with nodules and discharge.
Examination of the right ankle: Multiple ill-defined erythematous nodules, 2-3 cm in size, with serosanguinous discharge and right ankle swelling.
Examination of the right leg: A single annular hyperpigmented scaly patch over the right leg below the knee.
Temperature, regional nodes, and systemic examination: Afebrile, no regional lymphadenopathy, and a normal systemic examination.
Potassium hydroxide examination: Positive for fungal hyphae.
Histopathology of the nodule: Mixed inflammatory infiltrate of lymphocytes, macrophages, epithelioid cells, neutrophils, and plasma cells in the deep dermis, with few Langhans giant cells.
Fungal culture of the discharge: Growth of Trichophyton rubrum.
cases.final_diagnosis: Majocchi’s granuloma caused by Trichophyton rubrum following misuse of over-the-counter topical steroids

cases.case_summary: A 35-year-old woman is referred for corneal treatment, with visual acuity of counting fingers in front of the right eye and hand motions in front of the left eye.
cases.full_text:
A 35-year-old woman is referred for corneal treatment, with visual acuity of counting fingers in front of the right eye and hand motions in front of the left eye.
Prior ocular diagnoses: Bilateral Chandler syndrome and congenital glaucoma.
Glaucoma procedures and intraocular pressure: Prior trabeculotomy, selective laser trabeculoplasty, Ahmed Glaucoma Valve implantation, and trabeculectomy, with fluctuating intraocular pressure.
Visual acuity: Counting fingers in front of the right eye and hand motions in front of the left eye.
Corneal examination: Significant corneal opacity, oedema, peripheral scarring, and neovascularization in both eyes.
Anterior segment examination: Pseudopolycoria, corectopia, and hypotrophy of the iris in both eyes, seen once the corneas could be examined after penetrating keratoplasty.
Examination of the mother: Posterior embryotoxon in a transparent cornea and iris anomalies in her only eye, with best-corrected visual acuity 0.3; the other eye was prosthetic for an unknown reason.
DNA sequencing: Heterozygous pathogenic deletion covering a fragment of exon 1 and the entire 3′UTR of FOXC1 on one allele, present in the three sisters tested.
cases.final_diagnosis: Axenfeld-Rieger syndrome (ARS) caused by a novel FOXC1 gene mutation

cases.case_summary: An 8-year-old boy with no previous cardiac history and no remarkable personal or family history developed recurrent fever to 39.4°C, fatigue, vomiting, and abdominal pain over 3 days, then oliguria, confusion, and hypotension the day before admission.
cases.full_text:
An 8-year-old boy with no previous cardiac history and no remarkable personal or family history developed recurrent fever to 39.4°C, fatigue, vomiting, and abdominal pain over 3 days, then oliguria, confusion, and hypotension the day before admission.
Past medical and family history: No previous cardiac history and no remarkable personal or family history.
Cardiopulmonary examination: Rough and moist rales, muffled heart sounds, an irregular heart rhythm, and a gallop.
Serum laboratory studies: CRP, BNP, and NT-pro BNP were significantly elevated. CK, CK-MB, and troponin I were elevated.
Electrocardiogram: Widened QRS complex, ST-segment depression, premature ventricular complexes, and complete right bundle branch block.
Echocardiogram: Ejection fraction 28%, with mildly decreased right ventricular systolic function, mild mitral regurgitation, and mild/moderate tricuspid regurgitation. Atrial and ventricular internal diameters were not significantly enlarged, and the interventricular and left ventricular posterior walls were not markedly thickened.
Bronchoalveolar lavage metagenomic sequencing: Human rhinovirus type A was identified, with 3,540 reads covering 99% of the HRV A genome.
Rhinovirus phylogenetic analysis: The HRV-A strain subgrouped into A66.
Bacterial cultures: Bacterial culture of all samples yielded negative results.
cases.final_diagnosis: Fulminant myocarditis associated with human rhinovirus A66 infection

encounter.start: Surgical outpatient presentation with progressive right thigh swelling
encounter.cutoff: Histopathology of the excised specimen
encounter.cutoff_quote: Histopathology confirmed the diagnosis

findings.name: Prior care and associated history
findings.result: Conservative pain-relief treatment had been given at two primary healthcare facilities after a misdiagnosis. There was no sudden enlargement, trauma, or similar past lesions, and no fever, chills, or difficulty at work.
findings.quote: During previous visits to two primary healthcare facilities, he had received conservative treatment with pain relief medications following a misdiagnosis. There was no history of a sudden increase in the size of swelling, trauma, or similar lesions in the past. Additionally, he did not report any fever, chills, or difficulties at work.

findings.name: Physical examination
findings.result: General examination was unremarkable. A 12 × 9 × 7 cm firm, tender swelling was present on the outer aspect of the middle third of the right thigh, with pain worse while walking. The overlying skin was normal and movement was unrestricted.
findings.quote: A general physical examination was unremarkable. However, a thorough clinical evaluation revealed a 12 × 9 × 7 cm firm and tender swelling on the outer aspect of the middle third of the right thigh, with pain over the swelling, aggravated especially while walking. The skin over the swelling was normal, and there was no restriction in the range of movements.

findings.name: X-ray of the right thigh
findings.result: AP and lateral views showed no bone involvement, and the swelling was confined to the muscular compartment.
findings.quote: An X-ray of the right thigh (AP and lateral views) showed no bone involvement, with the swelling confined to the muscular compartment.

findings.name: Ultrasound of the right thigh
findings.result: A 12 × 8 × 8 cm complex, multiloculated cystic lesion in the middle third of the right thigh involved the vastus lateralis muscle belly.
findings.quote: Ultrasonography (USG) of the right thigh indicated a 12 × 8 × 8 cm complex, multiloculated cystic lesion in the middle third of the right thigh, involving the vastus lateralis muscle belly.

findings.name: MRI of the right thigh
findings.result: A cystic lesion with multiple internal daughter cysts measured 13.5 × 6.7 × 5.1 cm and involved the vastus lateralis. It was hypointense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images.
findings.quote: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the right thigh revealed a large cystic lesion with multiple internal daughter cysts, measuring 13.5 × 6.7 × 5.1 cm, involving the vastus lateralis muscle (Figure 1). The lesion appeared hypointense on T1 weighted image (T1WI) and hyperintense on T2WI images (Figure 2).

findings.name: Chest X-ray and ultrasound of the abdomen and pelvis
findings.result: No additional foci were seen in the chest, abdomen, or pelvis.
findings.quote: A chest X-ray and ultrasound of the abdomen and pelvis revealed no additional hydatidosis foci in the body.

findings.name: Gross inspection of the excised specimen
findings.result: Multiple daughter cysts were present when the specimen was opened.
findings.quote: Upon opening the specimen, multiple daughter cysts were identified

findings.name: Maternal blood group and crossmatch
findings.result: Group A, RhD-positive; crossmatch incompatible, with a compatible unit identified after six units were tested
findings.quote: the patient's blood group was found to be A RhD-positive. The cross-matching procedure was conducted using Bio-Rad column agglutination gel cards (Anti-IgG + Anti-C3d cards), and cross-matching was found to be incompatible. A total of six units were crossmatched and typed until a compatible unit was identified.

findings.name: Maternal direct Coombs test, autocontrol, and indirect Coombs test
findings.result: Direct Coombs test and autocontrol negative; indirect Coombs test positive
findings.quote: A direct Coombs test and autocontrol were also performed using Bio-Rad column agglutination gel cards and were found to be negative. An indirect Coombs test was performed, which was positive

findings.name: Maternal antibody identification, Duffy phenotype, and titer
findings.result: 2+ reactivity in panel cells 1, 3, 6, 9, 10, and 11; anti-Fya identified; maternal red cells Fya-b+; anti-Fya titer 8
findings.quote: 2+ cell reactivity was found in cell lines 1, 3, 6, 9, 10, and 11 of the Bio-Rad ID Dia 11-cell panel. Elucidation was done using the antigram provided by the manufacturer, and anti-Fya was identified in the maternal serum. Phenotyping of the mother’s red blood cells using anti-Fya serum revealed that she was Fya-b+. Titration was conducted to assess the level of anti-Fya antibodies in the maternal serum, which was found to be 8.

findings.name: Paternal red-cell Duffy typing
findings.result: Fya+b+
findings.quote: Phenotyping of the paternal RBC sample indicated the presence of Fya+b+ antigens.

findings.name: Newborn examination at delivery
findings.result: Live female infant weighing 2.75 kg; APGAR 8/10 at one minute and 9/10 at five minutes; pink and alert, no hydrops, and no abnormality on systemic examination
findings.quote: a live female baby weighing 2.75 kg was delivered. The APGAR (appearance, pulse, grimace, activity, and respiration) score was 8/10 at one minute and 9/10 at five minutes. Upon examination, the baby appeared pink, alert, and showed no signs of hydrops. Systemic examination also revealed no abnormalities.

findings.name: Cord-blood grouping, direct Coombs test, phenotype, and eluate
findings.result: Group A, RhD positive; polyspecific direct Coombs test 2+; red-cell phenotype Fya+b+; eluate showed anti-Fya
findings.quote: The baby’s blood group was found to be A RhD positive. The DCT, performed using a polyspecific (Anti-IgG + Anti-C3d) anti-human globulin Coombs gel card, showed a result of 2+. The baby’s RBCs were phenotyped by direct agglutination with anti-Fya and anti-Fyb reagents, revealing a phenotype of Fya+b+. Adsorption and elution were performed on the cord blood cells. Antibody identification using the Bio-Rad ID Dia 11-cell panel (894233.87.1) was done on the prepared eluate, confirming the presence of anti-Fya.

findings.name: Serum electrolytes, creatine kinase, and urine pH
findings.result: From 30 days before admission until the day before admission, serum potassium was 2.58–2.85 mmol/L, chloride 111.0–115.1 mmol/L, and carbon dioxide binding capacity 13.2–16.2 mmol/L, with a normal serum anion gap, normal creatine kinase, and urine pH 7–7.5.
findings.quote: From 30 days ago until the day before admission, laboratory findings revealed fluctuations in serum potassium (2.58-2.85mmol/L), chloride (111.0-115.1mmol/L), carbon dioxide binding capacity (13.2-16.2mmol/L), the serum anion gap was normal, creatine kinase (CK) levels were normal, and urine pH 7-7.5.

findings.name: Response to potassium chloride

findings.name: Arterial blood gas

findings.name: 24-hour urine biochemistry
findings.result: Sodium 78 mmol/L, potassium 33.96 mmol/L (reported as elevated), chloride 91.1 mmol/L, and calcium 1.85 mmol/L.

findings.name: Antinuclear antibody spectrum

findings.name: Lip gland biopsy and dryness symptoms
findings.result: On the eighth day after admission, lip gland biopsy showed mild lobular atrophy and scattered lymphocyte infiltration. There were no typical symptoms of dry mouth or dry eyes.
