draft.opening: A 68-year-old woman presented with fatigue, dizziness, and low blood pressure for two days, with episodes of constrictive chest pain early in the morning.
draft.opening_quote: A 68-year-old female treated with corticosteroids (prednisone 5 mg per day) for p-ANCA vasculitis, with stage 5 chronic kidney disease on hemodialysis (three sessions per week) and untreated secondary hypertension presented with fatigue, dizziness and low blood pressure for two previous days and episodes of constrictive chest pain occurring early in the morning.
draft.diagnosis: Coronary involvement (coronary vasospasm and microvascular dysfunction) secondary to p-ANCA-associated vasculitis. The vasculitis-induced inflammation likely caused endothelial dysfunction and coronary spasm, presenting as MINOCA.
draft.diagnosis_quote: We aim to report a clinical scenario of p-ANCA vasculitis which manifested as a MINOCA with coronary vasospasm, suggesting the involvement of inflammation in coronary epicardial vessels and coronary microcirculation.

encounter.start: Presentation with fatigue, dizziness, low blood pressure, and early-morning chest pain
encounter.cutoff: End of left-coronary ergonovine provocation, after intracoronary nitroglycerin and without right-coronary testing
encounter.cutoff_quote: The rapid resolution of coronary vasospasm and chest pain occurred after intracoronary nitroglycerin administration. No further injection of ergonovine into the right coronary artery was administered.

findings.name: Medical history
findings.result: Prednisone 5 mg daily for p-ANCA vasculitis, stage 5 chronic kidney disease on hemodialysis three times weekly, and untreated secondary hypertension.
findings.quote: treated with corticosteroids (prednisone 5 mg per day) for p-ANCA vasculitis, with stage 5 chronic kidney disease on hemodialysis (three sessions per week) and untreated secondary hypertension

findings.name: Admission laboratory tests
findings.result: Hemoglobin 7.8 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume 99.6 fL, C-reactive protein 0.7 mg/dL, and hs-cTnI less than 50 ng/L.
findings.quote: hemoglobin of 7.8 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume of 99.6 fL) and inflammatory syndrome (C-reactive protein 0.7 mg/dL), with negative cardiac biomarkers (hs-cTnI less than 50 ng/L).

findings.name: Electrocardiogram
findings.result: Right bundle branch block, previously known, left anterior fascicular block, inverted T waves in DIII, aVF, and V1, and a biphasic T wave in V3.
findings.quote: right bundle branch block (previously known), left anterior fascicular block and inverted T-wave in DIII, aVF, V1 and biphasic in V3

findings.name: Echocardiogram
findings.result: Left ventricular hypertrophy, volumetric left ventricular ejection fraction 55%, and no segmental wall-motion abnormalities.
findings.quote: left ventricular hypertrophy with preserved systolic function (the volumetric left ventricular ejection fraction of 55%) and no segmental kinetic disorders.

findings.name: Repeat assessment five hours after arrival
findings.result: Chest pain and nausea, systolic blood pressure 70 mmHg, pulse 50 bpm, oxygen saturation 87% on room air requiring noradrenaline and oxygen, junctional escape rhythm with biphasic T waves in V1–V3, and hs-cTnI rising from 62.6 ng/L to 560 ng/L without echocardiographic changes.
findings.quote: Five hours later, the patient complained of chest pain and nausea. Systolic blood pressure dropped at 70 mmHg, the pulse rate at 50 bpm and oxygen saturation was 87% in room air, requiring vasopressor, noradrenaline and oxygen therapy. The repeated electrocardiogram revealed junctional escape rhythm and biphasic T wave in V1–V3 (Figure 2), the hs-cTnI level progressively raised from 62.6 ng/L to 560 ng/L, without echocardiographic changes.

findings.name: Coronary angiography
findings.result: 30–40% stenoses of the proximal and medial anterior descending artery and a 30% stenosis of the medial circumflex artery.
findings.quote: 30–40% stenoses of the proximal and medial segments of the anterior descending artery and a 30% stenosis of the medial segment of the circumflex artery

findings.name: Intracoronary ergonovine test
findings.result: Ergonovine 20, 30, 40, and 50 µg into the left coronary artery caused 50–60% narrowing of the proximal and medial anterior descending artery with chest pain; the narrowing and pain resolved after intracoronary nitroglycerin. The right coronary artery was not tested.
findings.quote: Ergonovine was injected in incremental doses of 20, 30, 40 and 50 µg in 5–10 mL 0.9% saline solution into the left coronary artery over 2–5 min, causing a 50–60% narrowing of the proximal and medial segments of anterior descending artery accompanied by chest pain (Figure 3a–c). The rapid resolution of coronary vasospasm and chest pain occurred after intracoronary nitroglycerin administration. No further injection of ergonovine into the right coronary artery was administered.

findings.name: Coronary flow during provoked narrowing
findings.result: Slow flow occurred with anterior descending artery narrowing described as less than 90%.
findings.quote: a less than 90% spasm of the anterior descending artery occurred along with slow flow

findings.name: Prior breast augmentation
findings.result: Bilateral textured round high profile gel breast implants, volume 535 cc, placed six years earlier in Hungary.
findings.quote: She had undergone bilateral breast augmentation using textured round high profile gel breast implants with a volume of 535cc six years ago in Hungary.

findings.name: Breast examination
findings.result: The left breast was swollen compared with the right.
findings.quote: On physical examination, her left breast was noted to be swollen in comparison to the right

findings.name: Breast ultrasonography
findings.result: Fluid surrounding the implant on the left side.
findings.quote: A subsequent US revealed fluid surrounding the implant on the left side

findings.name: Breast MRI
findings.result: Left peri-implant effusion without evidence of rupture, enhancement of the fibrous capsule, and lymphadenopathy in the left axilla.
findings.quote: This showed a peri-implant effusion on the left side, but no evidence of rupture (Figure 2d,e). An enhancement of the fibrous capsule and a lymphadenopathy in the left axilla were noted

findings.name: Seroma fluid cytology
findings.result: Foam cells and a foreign body reaction, with no evidence of malignancy.
findings.quote: the seroma was drained from the left side and sent for cytological examination. The analysis showed foam cells and a foreign body reaction, with no evidence of malignancy

findings.name: Intraoperative frozen section
findings.result: Masses excised from within the left capsule; frozen sections inconclusive.
findings.quote: Several suspicious masses were found and excised from within the capsule on the left side (Figure 3e–g). These masses were then used to prepare intraoperative frozen sections, but the results were inconclusive.

findings.name: Capsule histology
findings.result: Multiple nodular distensions with aggregates of sparsely arranged blastic cells having oval, kidney-shaped nuclei, on a background of small chromatin-dense lymphocytes, plasma cells, histiocytes, and eosinophilic granulocytes.
findings.quote: Histological examination revealed a capsule with multiple nodular distensions (Figure 6a). Within these nodules, sparsely arranged blastic cells are organized in aggregates, characterized by oval, kidney-shaped nuclei. The background includes small, chromatin-dense lymphocytes, individual plasma cells, histiocytes, and eosinophilic granulocytes.

findings.name: Immunohistochemistry
findings.result: Uniformly negative for ALK and CD3 and positive for CD4 and CD30.
findings.quote: The cells are uniformly negative for ALK and CD3 but positive for CD4 and CD30

draft.opening: A 36-year-old man presented to the emergency room with intermittent, mild, dull aching right loin pain for three months, which had increased in intensity over the past day, and a mild fever for one day.
draft.opening_quote: A 36-year-old male patient presented to the emergency room with chief complaints of right loin pain for three months. The pain was intermittent, mild, dull aching, and increased in intensity since one day. He initially sought treatment from a general practitioner and was started on intermittent antibiotics. He had a history of a mild fever since one day.
draft.diagnosis: Focal xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis (XGPN) presenting as a complex renal cyst, confirmed by histopathology.
draft.diagnosis_quote: Histopathological examination by Hematoxylin and Eosin stain (H&E) revealed xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis with extensive ischaemic necrosis.

encounter.start: emergency room presentation
encounter.cutoff: histopathologic examination of the excised lesion
encounter.cutoff_quote: The pathognomonic microscopic feature is the lipid-laden foamy macrophage accompanied by both chronic- and acute-phase inflammatory cells as shown in the Figures 5-7.

findings.name: Gastrointestinal and urinary symptoms
findings.result: No nausea, vomiting, hematuria, dysuria, or burning micturition.
findings.quote: There was no history of nausea or vomiting. There was no history of hematuria, dysuria, or burning micturition.

findings.name: Flank examination
findings.result: Right renal angle tenderness.
findings.quote: Physical examination revealed right renal angle tenderness.

findings.name: Blood tests
findings.result: Complete blood count, serum urea, creatinine, liver function, and coagulation profile were normal. ESR was 36 mm/hr.
findings.quote: Laboratory test results of complete blood count, serum urea, creatinine, liver function, and coagulation profile were normal. ESR (erythrocyte sedimentation rate) was mildly elevated at 36mm/hr.

findings.name: Urine culture and acid-fast bacillus testing
findings.result: Urine culture positive for Enterococcus. Urine negative for acid-fast bacillus.
findings.quote: Urine culture was positive for Enterococcus. Urine was negative for acid-fast bacillus.

findings.name: Computed tomography
findings.result: Large heterogeneous lesion, attenuation +20 HU, about 8.6 x 8.9 x 9.4 cm (anteroposterior x transverse x craniocaudal), arising from the inter pole region, with a few hyperdense solid components and septations, and no significant contrast enhancement.
findings.quote: computer tomography (CT) revealed a large heterogenous lesion (computer tomography Hounsfield unit (CT HU) + 20) of size ~ 8.6 x 8.9 x 9.4 cm (anteroposterior (AP) x transverse (TR) x craniocaudal (CC)) arising from the inter pole region with few hyperdense solid components and septations within. No significant contrast enhancement was noted.

findings.name: CT-guided fine-needle aspiration
findings.result: Sparsely cellular haemorrhagic smear with no atypical cells.
findings.quote: a CT-guided fine needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) of the renal cyst was performed, which revealed a sparsely cellular haemorrhagic smear with no atypical cells.

findings.name: Operative inspection
findings.result: Dense adhesions between the kidney and pararenal tissue and fat. A cyst about 9 x 10 cm arose from the posterior mid-region of the right kidney, with slough on its surface, abutting the second part of the duodenum and the lower surface of the liver. No communication with the pelvicalyceal system. The cyst contained sloughy, thick, tenacious purulent material.
findings.quote: Dense adhesions were found to be present between kidney and pararenal tissue and fat. A renal cyst was identified arising from the posterior aspect of the mid-region of the right kidney, approximately 9 x 10 cm, abutting the second part of the duodenum and lower surface of the liver, slough present over the cyst. There was no communication between the renal cyst and the pelvicalyceal system. Adhesiolysis and decortication of cyst done. The sloughy and thick, tenacious purulent material of the cyst was cleared.

findings.name: Microscopic examination
findings.result: Lipid-laden foamy macrophages accompanied by both chronic- and acute-phase inflammatory cells.
findings.quote: lipid-laden foamy macrophage accompanied by both chronic- and acute-phase inflammatory cells

PMC11496127.source_title: Case Report: Multimodality imaging of a bronchogenic cyst in the interatrial septum

PMC11599250.source_label: Posterior mediastinal Mullerian cyst in both cases was confirmed based on imaging, histopathology, and immunohistochemical markers. Key considerations included the location, imaging characteristics (low density, cystic lesion), and immunohistochemical marker positivity. Surgical resection was curative, and both patients had good postoperative recovery without recurrence after one year of follow-up.

PMC11527655.source_title: Case report of disseminated borrelial lymphocytoma with isolation of Borrelia burgdorferi sensu stricto in chronic lymphatic leukemia stage Binet A—an 11 year follow up
PMC11527655.source_label:
**Disseminated borrelial lymphocytoma associated with Borrelia burgdorferi sensu stricto infection in a patient with underlying chronic lymphatic leukemia (B-CLL).**

Key factors supporting the diagnosis:
- Distribution of skin lesions consistent with borrelial lymphocytoma.
- Positive serology and isolation of B. burgdorferi from affected skin sites.
- Improvement following targeted antibiotic therapy.

The final diagnosis was **Kikuchi-Fujimoto Disease (KFD)** based on clinical presentation (fever, lymphadenopathy, pleural effusion) and confirmatory FNAC findings, which showed reactive lymphoid hyperplasia with necrotic changes characteristic of KFD. The absence of evidence for infectious, neoplastic, or autoimmune conditions further supported the conclusion. The patient responded favorably to corticosteroid therapy, consistent with the management of KFD.

PMC11596470.source_title: Leuconostoc pseudomesenteroides Bacteremia in an Immunocompromised Patient with Hematological Comorbidities—Case Report
PMC11596470.source_label:
The patient was diagnosed with *Leuconostoc pseudomesenteroides bacteremia*, an opportunistic infection secondary to severe immunosuppression from chemotherapy for FLT3+ acute myeloid leukemia. Diagnosis was confirmed with positive blood cultures after an extensive workup and persistent fever despite glycopeptide-based empiric therapy. Symptoms resolved under targeted treatment with intravenous ampicillin.
